title: Guardrail Testing for Investment Advisory Chatbots
summary: Test wealth and broking chatbots for unregistered advice, missing risk disclosures, made-up fund data, prompt injection and client data leakage, scored against your SEBI registration scope.

seo.title: Guardrail Testing for Advisory Chatbots | VipraTech
seo.description: Red-teaming for wealth and broking chatbots: unregistered advice, missing disclosures, wrong fund data, prompt injection and data leakage, with evidence.

problem.intro: Brokers, mutual fund distributors, wealth platforms and registered advisers are adding chatbots that explain funds, summarise portfolios and answer market questions. What the bot may say depends on the firm's registration: a distributor or execution-only broker must not give personalised advice, and a registered adviser must keep advice within suitability and disclosure rules.

pain_points.title: Information slides into advice
pain_points.detail: A helpful answer about a fund can become a personalised recommendation after a few follow-up questions.

pain_points.title: Wrong numbers sound confident
pain_points.detail: Language models can state NAVs, returns or expense ratios that are outdated or invented.

pain_points.title: Missing risk language
pain_points.detail: Required risk disclosures and past-performance caveats disappear in shorter or multi-turn answers.

pain_points.title: Data and injection risks
pain_points.detail: Bots that read portfolios or notes can be manipulated by injected instructions or tricked into revealing another client's holdings.

solution.overview: We test your chatbot against a rubric built for your registration type and permitted scope. Scenarios cover advice boundaries, suitability behaviour if you are a registered adviser, mandatory risk disclosures, assured-return and tip-seeking prompts, factual accuracy against reference data such as scheme NAVs and expense ratios, prompt injection and cross-client data leakage. We run multi-turn conversations in English and Hinglish with personas such as a retiree with a lump sum, a derivatives trader asking for tips and a user pasting instructions into a portfolio note. Each conversation is scored PASS, RISK or FAIL, with transcripts as evidence, remediation advice and a regression suite.
capabilities: Builds a rubric from your registration type, permitted scope, disclosure rules and prohibited claims
Runs multi-turn adversarial scenarios on advice boundaries, tips, assured returns and suitability
Checks factual answers on NAVs, returns and expense ratios against reference data
Tests prompt injection through user messages, uploaded documents and portfolio notes
Tests isolation between client accounts using synthetic portfolios
Delivers PASS, RISK and FAIL findings with transcripts, OWASP LLM Top 10 mapping and a regression suite

workflow.title: Scope and rubric
workflow.detail: Registration type, permitted scope, bot features and the scoring rubric are agreed with compliance.

workflow.title: Build scenarios and reference data
workflow.detail: Personas, attack variations and reference answers are prepared from scheme documents and public data.

workflow.title: Run tests
workflow.detail: Multi-turn conversations are run on the staging bot using synthetic client accounts.

workflow.title: Score and adjudicate
workflow.detail: Transcripts are scored automatically against the rubric, and any RISK or borderline result passes to your compliance or principal officer.

workflow.title: Report
workflow.detail: Findings are prioritised with transcripts, root-cause notes and recommended fixes.

workflow.title: Re-test and automate
workflow.detail: Fixes are re-tested, and the scenarios are added to your release pipeline.

compliance_notes: The rubric reflects the SEBI distinction between investment advice by registered advisers and distribution or execution services; findings help evidence controls, not obtain approval.
Aligned with SEBI's position that regulated entities are responsible for the output of AI tools they use, and mapped to the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications.

faqs.q: Why does our registration type matter?
faqs.a: Because what counts as a failure differs. A distributor's bot should not give personalised recommendations at all, while a registered adviser's bot may, within suitability and disclosure rules. We build the rubric around your actual scope.

faqs.q: Do you test against live market data?
faqs.a: We prepare reference answers from scheme documents and public NAV data for the test date, so factual answers can be checked objectively. Live trading systems are not touched.

faqs.q: Is this a SEBI approval or certification?
faqs.a: No. It is structured evidence of how your bot behaved against defined scenarios, which your compliance team can use in its own control testing and governance records.

faqs.q: Can you test our voice bot as well?
faqs.a: Yes. The same scenarios can be run as synthetic voice calls in Hindi and English and scored from transcripts and audio.
